name: FatDB
tagline: Short-lived .NET NoSQL store from FatCloud that sat alongside SQL Server; the company closed in 2014.
description: FatDB was a commercial distributed NoSQL database for Windows and .NET, released by FatCloud in 2012. It stored schema-free documents and key-value data across a cluster of Windows nodes with sharding and a configurable replication factor, and it was pitched as a way to extend existing Microsoft SQL Server applications rather than replace them. Developers worked in C# through a .NET client API with LINQ, a RESTful HTTP API or WCF RPC, and could run map/reduce jobs and server-side logic written as .NET code. There was no SQL interface of its own, no multi-record transactions and only application-level security. FatCloud ceased operations in February 2014 and the product disappeared with it.
statusNote: FatCloud ceased operations in February 2014 and FatDB was discontinued. RavenDB or Azure Cosmos DB serve the .NET NoSQL niche today.

pricing.notes: Commercial licence; the exact pricing terms have not survived. No longer sold.

scale.notes: Sharded across Windows nodes with a selectable replication factor.

strengths: Native .NET experience: LINQ queries and C# map/reduce
Designed to sit beside SQL Server rather than replace it
Sharding and replication on plain Windows servers
weaknesses: Vendor closed in 2014; no binaries, support or documentation remain
Windows-only, with no SQL, transactions or built-in access control
useCases: Context for legacy systems that once depended on FatDB
